# Memory context v1 served samples

Generated by `served_vectors::memory_context_v1_records_match_published_files`
through the real asynchronous handler with incarnation `0123456789abcdef` and
fixed clock 700. Successful reply bytes are embedded verbatim, not reserialized.
Only scratch filesystem prefixes in requests are normalized to `/fixture`.

- `context-project.json`: registered domain before a document, with revision 2,
  agentless/unplaced project, unregistered folder, and a Git worktree.
- `context-session.json`: live agents with and without a memory-profile pin, then
  the same pin after the registry revokes that version (`status` populated).
- `workspace-document.json`: latest, revision 1, and unknown revision refusal.

All reads use a reserved non-core caller, demonstrating that clients other than
core can read this data without special privileges. These
samples use sharing off (`logPosition: 0`); generation is the machine-local
journal head, not an agent version or shared position. See
[`docs/memory-context.md`](../../docs/memory-context.md) for schemas and hash
encoding. The session's `agent` object has the same limited `agent.resolve`
fields: agent_id, status, merged_into, gone and generation. It does not embed
the full identity row (name, tag, avatar or placement).

Regenerate from the repository root:

```
ENTO_WRITE_SERVED_VECTORS=1 cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked served_vectors::memory_context_v1_records_match_published_files
```

`SHA256SUMS` records the checksums of the three JSON files and this README;
recompute it after regeneration so consumers can verify their copies.
Without that environment variable, the test compares exact served bytes against
the committed files. Existing resolve/enumerate vectors remain unchanged.
